milestone_summary: Fidelity Electronics released Chess Challenger, the first dedicated chess computer sold to the public.

quote: He looked up from the book-screen, waiting.
claim_description: Reading books on a portable screen, with book-reels and adventure tapes as media.
concept_description: A portable screen device that displays the text of books and documents stored electronically in place of paper.
milestone_summary: Sony Data Discman DD-1, a handheld electronic book player reading books on mini-CD, sold in Japan in 1990

quote: For what have I got in the way of knowledge that […] hasn't got? After all, […] has been functioning for quite some time. It was given innumerable problems to digest and it has solved them with truly superhuman speed and efficiency.
claim_description: A giant brain-modelled electronic computer solves problems at superhuman speed, with a stated intelligence 25,000 times human intelligence.
concept_description: A computer built or programmed as many interconnected neuron-like units that together compute and learn, modelled on the brain.
milestone_summary: Bell Labs applied convolutional neural networks trained by backpropagation (LeNet) to handwritten digit recognition for zip codes, later reading cheques in ATMs.

quote: you were very wise, when you saw that a crash threatened, to lock the ship's machinery so that only your own personal characteristic motions would open it again.
claim_description: A spaceship security system that locks its machinery and opens only to one person's characteristic bodily motions.
concept_description: A card, disc or token encoded with a person's identity that machines read to grant access or check identity.
milestone_summary: The Rochester Institute of Technology 'VALI-DINE' system used cards with mechanically punched holes, read by machine, to let students into dining halls.

quote: The Menograph was one of […]'s earliest inventions, and entirely superseded the pen and pencil.
claim_description: A mind-writer device records thoughts directly from the brain onto tape, replacing pen, typewriter and stenographers.
concept_description: A machine that writes down a person's thoughts as text, or shows their mental images or dreams on a screen.
milestone_summary: Chang and Makin at UCSF decoded spoken sentences from ECoG signals into text with 3% word error rate.

quote: you don't see a picture and create a dramatic story around it. Instead, you get thrust into the picture, the situation, and you have to work out the solution—or suffer whatever consequences the particular environmental challenge has in store for you.
claim_description: An immersive virtual-reality-like test in which the subject lives a simulated scenario that is experienced as fully real.
concept_description: A machine that feeds a person's senses a computer-generated world convincing enough to feel real.
milestone_summary: Virtuality 1000SU VR systems launched in London in 1990 and sold to corporations (Ford, IBM, Mitsubishi, Olin) before the 1991 arcade version.

quote: These index cards might conceivably be transparent and so contrived as to give a photographic copy promptly whenever it was needed, and they could have an attachment into which would slip a ticket bearing the name of the locality in which the individual was last reported.
claim_description: Transparent index cards that yield instant photographic copies and carry a slot-in ticket recording each person's last reported location.
concept_description: Worn tags, implants or devices that report where a person or vehicle is to a monitoring system.
milestone_summary: Judge Jack Love persuaded Michael Goss to found NIMCOS, which built radio ankle transmitters used to monitor offenders from a telephone-linked receiver.
